key_insight: Reducing memory to delayed feedback enables optimistic online optimization that adapts to both environmental change and prediction accuracy under time-varying constraints.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports stateful online learning and non-stochastic control with budget constraints, using potentially unreliable predictions to improve performance.
method: Reduce memory effects to delay and treat state-dependent gradients as delayed feedback.
Use optimistic updates to incorporate untrusted predictions.
Bound dynamic regret and cumulative constraint violation in terms of path length and prediction accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, including O(1) regret under perfect predictions and cumulative constraint violation of O(√T) for unknown path length or O(log T) for known or online-observable path length; no empirical evaluation is described.
watch_item: The stronger constraint-violation guarantee requires known or online-observable path length, which may be unavailable in deployment.
paper_title: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence
